headline: US Democrats funded 'anti-Argentina campaign' during World Cup, claims President Milei
summary: Argentine President Javier Milei has claimed a 'well-orchestrated anti-Argentina campaign' during the World Cup, involving criticism of the national team, racism accusations, and conspiracy theories. He alleges this campaign was funded by the US Democratic Par
details: President Javier Milei claims a "well-orchestrated 'anti-Argentina campaign'" during the World Cup, alleging criticism of the national team, racism accusations, and conspiracy theories about FIFA favoring Lionel Messi. He asserts that this campaign was funded by the US Democratic Party and the governments of Brazil and Mexico.

Milei, a self-proclaimed libertarian, stated on a local radio station that this was the work of "progressive minds who do not want free thought to succeed." He specifically accused the Brazilian government, led by leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, of providing the largest share of the funding.

Argentine analysts suggest Milei is using this narrative to divert attention from his rapidly declining popularity, while others argue that Milei himself is running an "anti-Argentina campaign" with his harsh austerity policies. The narrative has surprisingly resonated, even with those who don't support Milei.

A 52-year-old bookseller in Buenos Aires, who never voted for Milei, expressed anger and annoyance at the "aggressive campaign" against the country on social media. He criticized "imperialist powers" for making racism accusations, denying Black people's existence in Argentina, and ignoring their history.

During the World Cup, incidents of racist behavior by some Argentine fans gained widespread attention, with American actor Samuel L. Jackson urging Black friends not to cheer for Argentina, calling it one of the most racist countries. Human rights organizations like Amnesty International Argentina acknowledged racism but criticized stereotyping the country.

Milei, however, blamed Argentina's opposition for legitimizing the "woke movement" now accusing them of racism. He later accused Brazil while in Brazil, attending the campaign launch of right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, where he called Lula da Silva a "thief" and a "convict," leading to strong reactions.

He reiterated his claims, stating, "If you examine the data of the recent anti-Argentine campaign, you will see that most of the attacks came from Brazil." On Sunday, he further emphasized this, adding Mexico and the US Democratic Party to his accusations.

Digital anthropologist Mercedes Maspero analyzed over 2 million social media posts, finding "undeniable patterns" of organized conduct, such as repeated use of variations of "horrible people" in different languages. However, she found it "quite difficult" to label it a "well-organized campaign" due to its "incredible spread."

Natalia Aruguete, a researcher working on social media and political agendas, also found "no evidence of a large-scale organized campaign," despite a "hostile, widespread, and transnational discussion" around Argentina. She noted a significant Brazilian presence in racism discussions but "no public evidence" supporting Milei's claims of Brazilian government involvement.

headline_marked: [[Witness tells tribunal Taposh and Nanak ordered attacks]] on July uprising protesters
headline: Witness tells tribunal Taposh and Nanak ordered attacks on July uprising protesters
summary: A prosecution witness testified that armed activists attacked protesters in Dhaka on the instructions of former DSCC mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh and former lawmaker Jahangir Kabir Nanak, leading to deaths.
details: A prosecution witness told the International Crimes Tribunal-1 that armed Awami League, Jubo League, and Chhatra League activists attacked protesters in Dhanmondi and Mohammadpur during the July uprising. The witness, Wasif Munim, alleged these attacks were carried out on the instructions of former DSCC mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh and former lawmaker Jahangir Kabir Nanak.

Munim recounted seeing his classmate, Farhan Fayaz, shot in the chest on July 18, 2024, who later died of his injuries. He also claimed police attacked protesters that day and that former DMP commissioner Habibur Rahman and official Biplob Kumar failed to take legal action.

In a separate case, witness NRB Mamun, a Jubo Dal activist, described a deadly attack on protesters in Narayanganj on July 19. He testified that Shamim Osman, his son Ayan Osman, nephew Ajmeri Osman, and around 100 armed Awami League activists were involved, leaving him injured by rubber bullets.

Mamun stated that two protesters, Adil and Yeasin, were shot dead on the spot. He also witnessed another protester, Swajon, being shot, allegedly by Ayan Osman, who later succumbed to his injuries after being refused treatment at a Narayanganj hospital, reportedly on Shamim Osman’s instructions.

Meanwhile, in a third case, former Agailjhara Police Sub-Inspector Monoranjan Mistry told ICT-2 that then Barishal SP AKM Ehsanullah ordered him to participate in a "crossfire" operation. Mistry claimed Ehsanullah stated the order came from then Awami League lawmaker Abul Hasanat Abdullah.

Mistry testified that he refused the order and was threatened with career ruin. He later learned that Tipu Hawlader and Kabir Mollah were killed in the alleged crossfire. Abul Hasanat Abdullah, AKM Ehsanullah, and two former ASIs are accused in this case.
caption:
